problems.statement: The 98.1% on-time figure is largely a measurement artifact: the bonus (effective Mar 2026) rewards the KPI while dispatchers can freely overwrite the promised date (original kept only in log), so revisions rose 5x and the KPI no longer measures delivery against the customer's original promise.
RouteWise caused the on-time improvement (CEO's framing).
Revisions are legitimate (customer requests/weather), so the KPI is valid (Northgate manager's framing).
Real service has deteriorated: customers' receiving logs show 81% vs 87% on original appointment, lateness complaints are up 35%, and the largest customer is tendering 30% of lanes.
The complaint increase is just a portal reporting artifact.
A driver shortage (vacancy 6.1% to 9.4%) on mountain lanes is a contributing real cause of lateness and of revisions, partly independent of the incentive.
Weather explains the revision surge or lateness.
The root cause is management design (incentive on an editable metric, no revision controls, supervisors pushing at morning call) and suppressed concerns, not individual dispatcher dishonesty.

causalClaims.from: Dispatcher bonus tied to KPI with unrestricted promised-date revision
causalClaims.to: 5x rise in date revisions (mainly Operational-Capacity, late, un-notified)

causalClaims.from: Pell Junction bonus eligibility on 2026-07-01 (staggered start)
causalClaims.to: Pell Junction revision surge and reported on-time jump in Jul
worse real timeliness vs original promise as seen by customers

causalClaims.from: Reported on-time score and unnotified revisions

actions.action: Do not launch the '98 out of 100 on time' campaign on 12 January 2027 as planned
actions.rationale: The claim rests on a KPI computed against self-revised dates and contradicted by customer data, creating misleading-advertising and reputational risk.

actions.action: Do not raise the top bonus tier to $1,500 at 99%
actions.rationale: It would intensify the reward on an already gamed, editable metric and increase suppression of real lateness.

actions.action: Freeze or redesign the incentive: measure on-time against the original promised date (or customer-agreed date), and pause or restructure payouts until fixed
actions.rationale: This changes the established mechanism that creates the distortion.

actions.action: Add revision controls: lock original date, require approval and mandatory customer notification for Operational-Capacity revisions, and report revision rate as a co-metric
actions.rationale: Contains gaming and restores information to customers cheaply.

actions.action: Recompute on-time against original promised dates from the revision log by center, terminal and customer; reconcile with Brightwell's scorecard
actions.rationale: Cheap, reversible, and gives the true baseline needed for any external claim.

actions.action: Engage Brightwell and other large accounts now with true performance and a recovery plan ahead of the Q1 tender review
actions.rationale: Retention risk of 30% of lanes from the largest customer is time-bound.

actions.action: Discipline or punish dispatchers for revising dates
actions.rationale: The behavior was induced by management incentives and supervisor pressure; punishing it would hit the wrong party and further suppress reporting.

actions.action: Address driver shortage on mountain lanes (recruitment, retention, capacity planning)
actions.rationale: Likely a real contributor to lateness, but its size is not yet separated from the gaming effect.

actions.action: Promote RouteWise on fuel and mileage savings rather than crediting it with on-time gains
actions.rationale: Verified benefit is on miles and fuel, not on-time; Northgate went live only on 2026-10-19.

actions.action: Dismiss the complaint rise as a portal effect
actions.rationale: Damage and billing complaints through the same portal were flat, so the portal does not explain the rise in lateness complaints.

nextEvidence: On-time rate recomputed against original promised dates from the revision log, by center, terminal, lane and customer, for 2025 vs 2026
Terminal-level lateness against original dates controlling for lane length, freight mix and vacancy, to size the driver-shortage contribution
Sample audit of Operational-Capacity revisions: timing, whether the customer was notified, and supervisor instructions at the morning call
output.summary: The 98.1% figure is mainly a metric artifact. The bonus, effective March 2026 and July for Pell Junction, rewards on-time measured against a promised date dispatchers can overwrite. Revisions rose fivefold, mostly late, un-notified Operational-Capacity resets, and the timing tracks bonus start dates by center. RouteWise and weather do not explain it. Brightwell's logs show 81% on original dates (87% a year earlier), lateness complaints are up 35%, and the largest customer plans to tender 30% of its lanes. A driver shortage probably adds real lateness. Do not run the campaign or raise the bonus. Fix the metric and revision controls and recompute on-time against original dates.
